# The honest part

## Julia moved the problem, it did not remove it

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- 82 of 396 issues and pull requests are about autodiff or numerics.
  There is a CI job per backend and a maintained list of what is broken
- The default solver is `GaussLegendre(; n = 64)`, not `QuadGKJL()`,
  because fixed nodes trace through every backend and adaptive ones do
  not
- Stan gave up adaptive quadrature for an ODE solver. Julia gave up
  adaptive quadrature for a 64 node dot product
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The first proper measurement of this package, April 2026, found four
  of six backend configurations broken or only partly working
- `try`/`catch` had to be taken **out** to unblock Mooncake. In Stan the
  complaint was that there is none to put in
- `logpdf` is a central difference of `logcdf` with a step hardcoded at
  `1e-8`, which is why finite differences cannot be the test reference
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
In Stan the workarounds are for the language. In Julia they are for the
autodiff backends.
:::

## R wins this, by about a hundred to one

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
|  | R | Julia |
|---|---:|---:|
| Downloads, all time | 11,211 | 116 |
| Downloads, last month | 511 | 49 |

::: {.attribution}
CRAN and JuliaPkgStats, 10 August 2026. Both counts include continuous
integration and mirrors, so neither is a count of people.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
- Four R packages use primarycensored, and three of the four are ours
- Every dependant of CensoredDistributions.jl is mine, Sam Brand's or
  Sebastian Funk's. I went looking for one from outside and did not
  find it
- primarycensored turns up in public health delay estimation, but the
  guide that recommends it is a guide we wrote
- Last month is the only number moving the right way, 49 against 511
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
The two packages are a month apart in age. The difference is the
ecosystem each landed in, not the language.
:::
